question.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+5}}⟨2t,\,2,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
question.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2t}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+5}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+5}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+5}})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{10}{(4{t}^{2}+5)^{3/2}},\,-\frac{8t}{(4{t}^{2}+5)^{3/2}},\,\frac{4t}{(4{t}^{2}+5)^{3/2}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{(4{t}^{2}+5)^{3/2}}⟨5,\,-4t,\,2t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{2}{(4{t}^{2}+5)^{3/2}}\sqrt{(5)^{2}+(-4t)^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{(4{t}^{2}+5)^{3/2}}\sqrt{25+16{t}^{2}+4{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{(4{t}^{2}+5)^{3/2}}\sqrt{20{t}^{2}+25} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{(4{t}^{2}+5)^{3/2}}\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+5} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{4{t}^{2}+5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{2}{(4{t}^{2}+5)^{3/2}}⟨5,\,-4t,\,2t⟩}{(\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{4{t}^{2}+5})}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+5}}⟨5,\,-4t,\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+5}}⟨2t,2,-1⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+5}}⟨5,\,-4t,\,2t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(4{t}^{2}+5)}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & 2 & -1 \\ 5 & -4t & 2t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(4{t}^{2}+5)}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -4t & 2t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2t & -1 \\ 5 & 2t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 2 \\ 5 & -4t\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(4{t}^{2}+5)}⟨4t-4t,-(4{t}^{2}+5),-8{t}^{2}-10⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}(4{t}^{2}+5)}⟨0,\,-(4{t}^{2}+5),\,-2(4{t}^{2}+5)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨0,\,-1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$
